title: ART + INSIGHT
location: Raclin Murphy Museum of Art | Main Building | Notre Dame, 46556
description: Engage with art, connect with others, and explore new perspectives in Art + Insight, a program designed for adults 55+. Through guided close-looking exercises, lively conversations, and shared experiences, we will discover fresh ways to engage with art while building community. Join us each month for meaningful discussions and creative inspiration in the galleries as we explore new works of art together. Parking is available in the Visitor Lot immediately north of the Sculpture Park for a fee during the week (before 4:30 p.m.) . Free two-hour parking is available in the Eddy Street Commons Parking Garage or along Angela Blvd. After 4:30 p.m. and on weekends, parking is free and available in any non-gated campus lot. If traveling via South Bend Transpo, take the No.7 bus and use the Eddy St. Commons stop. Originally published at raclinmurphymuseum.nd.edu.

title: BLOOD SIMPLE (1984)
location: DeBartolo Performing Arts Center, 100 Performing Arts Center | Notre Dame, 46556
description: Crime, Blood, and Laughs: The Coen Brothers Directed by Joel Coen With John Getz, Frances McDormand, Dan Hedaya Rated R, 96 minutes, Blu-ray This razor-sharp modern film noir, the first film by Joel and Ethan Coen, introduced the brothers' inimitable black humor and eccentric sense of character, a sensibility that has helped shape the course of contemporary American cinema. Deep in the heart of Texas, a sleazy bar owner suspects his wife of having an affair and hires a private detective to confirm his suspicions—only to have the crosshairs turned back on himself. Playfully shot by Barry Sonnenfeld and featuring a haunting score by Carter Burwell and a cunning performance by Frances McDormand, Blood Simple was a career-launching film for this ensemble and the first articulation of the precision of style that has defined the Coens' work ever since. Sponsored by the Meg and John P. Brogan Endowment for Classic Cinema.

title: MONIKA HERZIG ACOUSTIC PROJECT
location: Merrimans’ Playhouse | 401 E. Colfax Ave., Suite 135 | South Bend, IN 46617
description:
Composer and pianist Monika Herzig leads her quartet featuring guitarist Peter Kienle in a program centered on original compositions from her latest release, Transparent (2026), alongside selections from her extensive catalog of original recordings spanning more than two decades. Her music blends contemporary jazz with lyrical composition, inventive improvisation, and diverse musical influences, creating a distinctive artistic voice that continues to evolve through each recording project. Featuring original works by Herzig and selected compositions by guitarist Peter Kienle, the ensemble balances thoughtfully crafted compositions with dynamic ensemble interaction and spontaneous improvisation.

Monika Herzig - piano

Peter Kienle - bass

John Valdez - drums

title: OBSESSION (2025)
location: DeBartolo Performing Arts Center, 100 Performing Arts Center | Notre Dame, 46556
description: New at the Browning Directed by Curry Barker With Michael Johnston, Inde Navarrette, Cooper Tomlinson Rated R, 109 minutes, DCP When a film is made for less than $1,000,000 and makes over half a billion dollars at the box office, then it's a safe call that society is at some level obsessed with it. What made and continues to make this story about burgeoning romance that grows into something horrific such a cultural touchstone? While unpacking that, either come see again or catch up with ingénue Curry Barker's story of a wish for true love that pitches into a truly scary relationship

title: SEPTEMBER FIRST FRIDAYS: DOG DAYS OF SUMMER
location: S. Michigan Street, Downtown, South Bend | 100 & 200 Blocks of S. Michigan Street | South Bend, IN 46601
description:
Downtown South Bend will be going to the dogs for the September First Fridays, as we celebrate the "Dog Days of Summer." Bring your furry friend downtown for a fun night out!

We will have booths with animal rescue groups and organizations who provide goods and services for animals, as well as the opportunity to dine with your dog at one of our over 20 downtown pet-friendly patios. Also, if you want to dress up your pup in a costume or outfit, we will be handing out prizes to the best dressed dogs! We encourage people to grab some takeout from their favorite downtown eatery or First Fridays food vendor and enjoy it at the seating area in the street, where we also have vendors and live music by The Starving Artists. Plus Over the Edge returns to Studebaker Plaza, with fearless philanthropists rappelling over the edge of the Robertson's Apartment Building to raise money for Youth Service Bureau (YSB.) We will also have an EV Display near the State Theater, the South Bend Music Festival, plus lots of other fun happenings throughout downtown!
